title: FSDP2 pre-backward hook dropped by a view-returning forward
scope_and_topology: Two Gloo ranks on one host, FSDP2 over a CPU DeviceMesh during Phase B bring-up. Not multi-node evidence.
hypothesis: None declared in advance; this was not an experiment. A latent defect in this repository's own model was surfaced by a framework diagnostic.
detection_signal: An unsolicited UserWarning from torch.distributed.fsdp on the first sharded forward pass, stating that the wrapped module returned a view tensor and that an in-place op on it would silently drop the pre-backward hook and skip the all-gather.
injection: Not injected. SpatiotemporalTransformer.forward returned the result of .permute(), which is a view.
detection_evidence: The warning fired on every rank on the first fully_shard forward during Phase B bring-up and does not appear after the fix.
diagnosis: The failure is conditional and silent: nothing fails at the point of the view, the corruption requires a later in-place op, and the symptom is wrong gradient values rather than a crash, shape error or NaN. On a single GPU there is no all-gather to skip and the bug does not exist, so it would have appeared only under sharded execution and presented as the multi-node run converging worse than the single-GPU reference, a symptom with several plausible and wrong explanations.
intervention: Append .contiguous() to the forward's return value so no downstream in-place op can detach the hook. Documented in-line as load-bearing, since .contiguous() reads like a performance tweak and would otherwise be a tempting deletion.

verification.detail: The bit-exact resume oracle runs against the fixed model under FSDP2 and passes with zero differences across 186 tensors. This establishes a self-consistent reproducible sharded trajectory; it does not by itself prove the bug is gone, since the oracle compares two runs of the same code.

counterfactual: Had the warning been suppressed or ignored, the defect would have survived until a model change introduced an in-place op on the output, at which point gradients would have been quietly wrong on sharded runs only. The natural debugging path leads away from the cause, and the single-GPU reference would have looked perfect throughout.
limitations: Found by reading a framework warning, not by a detector this project built; no credit is claimed for the detection mechanism. The fix is verified by absence of the warning and by the bit-exactness oracle passing; a direct test asserting gradient equality between sharded and unsharded execution is NOT implemented and would be stronger evidence. One host, CPU, Gloo; not multi-node evidence.
